title: Databricks merge issue with null values
question:
I'm merging two delta tables with databricks and one struct in the target delta table isn't merged as expected.

On the source delta table I have data as follow:

{
  id: '123',
  artist: {
    song: {
      id: null,
      name: null,
      country: null
    }
  }
}

My goal is to extract the song, and set it directly as null if its id is null. To do so I do a select on the source table before merging:

self.spark.read.option("mode", "PERMISSIVE")
  .json(pattern, schema=artistSchema)
  .select(
    col('id'),
    when((col("artist.song").isNull() | col("artist.song.id").isNull()), lit(None)
        .otherwise(col("artist.song")).alias("song")
  )

When testing the select on its own, it gives me the expected data:

{
  id: '123',
  song: null
}

The issue arise when doing the merge afterwards using this (supposedly valid) data. Instead of {song: null} it merges with {song: {id: null, name: null, country: null}}

Here is how I do my merge:

deltaTable = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, deltaPath)
        deltaTable.alias("existing") \
            .merge(
                dataDf.alias("updates"), # dataDf is the "selected" input
                "existing.id = updates.id")
            .whenMatchedUpdateAll("(updates.song IS NOT DISTINCT FROM existing.song) OR (updates.song IS NOT NULL AND updates.song.id != existing.song.id OR updates.song.name != existing.song.name OR updates.song.country != existing.song.country)")
            .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
            .execute()

Since I can test the select on its own and it seems to provide valid data, I can only see an issue with the merge itself. What could cause this modification of the song struct ?
answer:
I think you need to be more explicit in your upsert code. This example is based on the examples in the Delta Lake Quickstart.

Prepare

First we prepare for this example by constructing a pair of delta tables (i.e., old and new data) on local disk by writing json files, reading them back in, and then writing out as delta.

Old Data

json_path_0 = "/tmp/json_0.json"

json_contents_0 = """
[{'id':'A','artist':{'song':{'id':'A','name':'name 1','country':'country 1'}}}]
[{'id':'B','artist':{'song':{'id':'B','name':'name 2','country':'country 2'}}}]
[{'id':'C','artist':{'song':{'id':'C','name':'name 3','country':'country 3'}}}]
"""

dbutils.fs.put(json_path_0, json_contents_0, overwrite = True)

df_0 = spark.read.json(json_path_0)

delta_path_0 = "/tmp/delta_0"

df_0.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").option('overWriteSchema', True).save(delta_path_0)

New Data

json_path_1 = "/tmp/json_1.json"

json_contents_1 = """
[{'id':'B','artist':{'song':{'id':null,'name':null,'country':null}}}]
[{'id':'D','artist':{'song':{'id':'D','name':'name 4','country':'country 4'}}}]
"""

dbutils.fs.put(json_path_1, json_contents_1, overwrite = True)

df_1 = spark.read.json(json_path_1)

delta_path_1 = "/tmp/delta_1"

df_1.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").option('overWriteSchema', True).save(delta_path_1)

Upsert

Then we can actually perform the requested upsert.

from delta.tables import *
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

# delta.tables.DeltaTable
dt_0 = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_path_0)

# pyspark.sql.dataframe.DataFrame
df_1 = spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path_1)

# upsert
dt_0.alias("old_data") \
  .merge(df_1.alias("new_data"), "old_data.id = new_data.id") \
  .whenMatchedUpdate(set = { "artist": when(col("new_data.artist.song.id").isNull(), lit(None)).otherwise(col("new_data.artist")) }) \
  .whenNotMatchedInsert(values = { "id": col("new_data.id"), "artist": col("new_data.artist") }) \
  .execute()

Results

And view the results.

dt_0.toDF().show()

+--------------------+---+
|              artist| id|
+--------------------+---+
|{{country 1, A, n...|  A|
|{{country 3, C, n...|  C|
|                NULL|  B|
|{{country 4, D, n...|  D|
+--------------------+---+
